governanceNotes: D1 batch 49 (2026-09-24): deferred. Synonym-identity screen recorded 2026-09-24: iritis is the traditional clinical term for inflammation of the iris and is used interchangeably with anterior uveitis in the ophthalmic literature, and the catalog carries the separately published uveitis identity, which already authors glaucoma (uveitis -> glaucoma, association-only) and cataracts (uveitis -> cataracts, association-only) windows; authoring iritis-to-glaucoma or iritis-to-cataracts edges would therefore restate the same disease process under a second identity name and create a parallel pathway, which is the disposition pattern applied to eczema, intervertebral-disc-syndrome, and other synonym pairs in this program.

Evidence and treatment-state screen recorded 2026-09-24: the located condition-specific literature measures complications in anterior uveitis and in anatomical subtypes of uveitis - for example the 2025 American Journal of Ophthalmology study of the incidence and prevalence of glaucoma, corticosteroid response, and ocular hypertension in uveitis and its anatomical subtypes, the 2023 American Journal of Ophthalmology study of cataract incidence in anterior uveitis, and the 2017 study of secondary glaucoma risk factors in herpetic anterior uveitis - and those outcomes are exactly the windows the uveitis identity already carries; the cataract and ocular-hypertension outcomes in that evidence are substantially corticosteroid-related, so an iritis window would additionally depend on the treatment state rather than the disease, which this program declines to author (treatment-state guard). Current evidence-ground guard: an iritis-primary proposition about visual impairment would run through the glaucoma and cataract intermediates that the uveitis identity owns (intermediate-chain guard), so no such edge is authored. Reopening condition: a governance decision that separates this identity from uveitis, or a catalog-fit outcome for iritis that the uveitis identity does not already author.
